title: The documents said a live run costs a few cents, and it costs about a dollar
foundBy: session agent, while reading the cost that a replayed run's trajectories show

evidence.verified: Read from the trajectories of the committed recording: orchestrator $0.72, developer $0.30 and qa $0.17, which is $1.19 for the campaign. The exported session of the small cassette comes to $0.0238 in total. Both are the agent's own accounting from recorded token counts, and neither was checked against a provider invoice.

details:
The README, the contributing guide, the Makefile help and two scripts all said that a live campaign costs a few cents. They also said that the small cassette costs a fraction of a cent. Nobody had measured either figure, and both came from the first draft of the README.

A recorded response carries the provider's token counts, so the trajectories show what a recording cost. The orchestrator resends its whole conversation on each of about sixty requests, and a late one holds over 60,000 prompt tokens.

A reader deciding whether to run step 7 was told a price more than ten times too low. Every figure now comes from a measurement, and the README says why a replayed run's trajectories still show a cost.
